headline: Tropical Equatorial Peatland Demarcation and Land Use Analysis in Borneo's Pontianak Delta Using Geospatial Approach
name: Tropical Equatorial Peatland Demarcation and Land Use Analysis in Borneo's Pontianak Delta Using Geospatial Approach
description: This investigation addresses critical deficiencies in Indonesian Indicative Map of Delay in Granting New Permits (IMDGNP) peatland boundary estimations through systematic verification of peat soil distributions in Pontianak City, West Kalimantan Province. Preliminary IMDGNP cartographic products at 1:250,000 scale identified four administrative districts containing peatland formations totaling 23.8649 km² , exhibiting documented accuracy limitations requiring comprehensive field validation. The research methodology integrated systematic field reconnaissance encompassing 614 observation points at 250-meter intervals, laboratory classification testing of 68 undisturbed soil specimens following ASTM D4427 (organic content > 75% threshold) and ASTM D2974 (ash content < 25% threshold) standardized procedures, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) spatial analysis for refined boundary demarcation at 1:50,000 scale. Results demonstrate that peat soil formations are confined to only two districts —Southeast Pontianak (5.798 km² , 35.95% of district area) and North Pontianak (17.320 km² , 42.14% of district area) —contrary to preliminary four -district estimations. Contrary to the preliminary four -district IMDGNP estimate of 23.8649 km² , verified peatland formations total 23.118 km² and are confined to only two districts. Within North Pontianak District specifically, the verified extent (17.320 km² ) exceeds the preliminary district-level IMDGNP estimate (12.7683 km² ) by 35.76%, while Pontianak City and East Pontianak districts contain organic soils rather than peat formations. The updated demarcation mapping incorporates peat layer depth information within a comprehensive geospatial database suitable for infrastructure planning , foundation design optimization, and building conserv ation, thereby supporting evidence -based urban development and environmental management aligned with tropical peatland ecosystem governance principles.

hasPart.name: 1. INTRODUCTION
hasPart.description: This section introduces the background and objectives of the study regarding tropical equatorial peatland demarcation and land use analysis in Borneo's Pontianak Delta. It highlights critical deficiencies in existing permit map estimations and outlines the importance of systematic verification for sustainable environmental management.

hasPart.name: 2. RESEARCH METHODS
hasPart.description: This section describes the methodologies applied in the study, including the study area, field investigation, data collection, and sampling strategies. It also outlines the procedures for organic and ash content testing, along with Geographic Information System (GIS) analysis and research flowcharts.

hasPart.name: 2.1 Study area
hasPart.description: This subsection provides a geographical overview of the study area within the Pontianak Delta in Borneo. It details the regional characteristics and administrative districts relevant to the peatland investigation.

hasPart.name: 2.2 Field investigation and data collection
hasPart.description: This subsection outlines the field investigation protocols and data collection techniques used on-site. It details the procedures implemented to gather primary data from targeted peatland zones.

hasPart.name: 2.3 Sampling strategy
hasPart.description: This subsection explains the strategic approach used for selecting sample points across the study region. It establishes the criteria and framework for comprehensive soil and environmental sampling.

hasPart.name: 2.3.1 Sampling location determination
hasPart.description: This subsection describes the specific methods and rationale utilized to determine exact sampling locations in the field. It ensures spatial representativeness across the verified peatland areas.

hasPart.name: 2.3.2 Field sampling procedures
hasPart.description: This subsection details the step-by-step procedures followed during the physical acquisition of soil samples. It ensures consistency and accuracy in handling and retrieving field data.

hasPart.name: 2.4 Organic content and ash content testing
hasPart.description: This subsection outlines the laboratory testing methods used to determine organic matter and ash content in the collected soil samples. These tests are essential for classifying peat soil properties.

hasPart.name: 2.5 Geographic Information System analysis
hasPart.description: This subsection introduces the framework for spatial analysis utilizing Geographic Information System (GIS) tools. It sets up the digital environment for processing spatial layers and mapping peatland boundaries.

hasPart.name: 2.5.1 Spatial data components
hasPart.description: This subsection identifies the various spatial data layers and datasets incorporated into the GIS environment. It details the primary and secondary inputs used for geospatial modeling.

hasPart.name: 2.5.2 Geographic Information System development and processing
hasPart.description: This subsection describes the technical processing steps and software workflows implemented to build the GIS database. It explains how spatial overlays and database queries were executed.

hasPart.name: 2.6 Research flowchart
hasPart.description: This subsection presents a structured diagrammatic flowchart summarizing the entire research methodology. It visually outlines the progression from data collection to final spatial evaluation.

hasPart.name: 3. RESULTS AND ANALYSIS
hasPart.description: This section presents the comprehensive findings derived from field investigations, laboratory testing, and geospatial mapping. It evaluates land use assessments, peat soil layer depths, and comparative map analyses.

hasPart.name: 3.1 Field investigation results
hasPart.description: This subsection details the primary outcomes obtained directly from the field surveys across the study zones. It provides initial insights into ground-level conditions and preliminary peat distributions.

hasPart.name: 3.1.1 Preliminary peatland distribution from Indicative Map of Delay in Granting New Permits map
hasPart.description: This subsection evaluates the initial peatland distribution patterns derived from the Indicative Map of Delay in Granting New Permits (IMDGNP). It highlights baseline assumptions prior to on-site verification.

hasPart.name: 3.1.2 Land use classification results
hasPart.description: This subsection presents the classification categories and spatial extents of various land uses identified within the study area. It maps human activities and vegetation covers overlapping with potential peat zones.

hasPart.name: 3.2 Laboratory classification results
hasPart.description: This subsection summarizes the analytical results obtained from laboratory soil testing. It establishes the physical and chemical benchmarks used for soil classification.

hasPart.name: 3.2.1 Organic content testing results
hasPart.description: This subsection details the quantified percentages of organic matter found across the analyzed soil samples. It confirms the organic composition thresholds characteristic of true peat soils.

hasPart.name: 3.2.2 Ash content testing results
hasPart.description: This subsection reports the ash content measurements determined through laboratory combustion procedures. It provides additional diagnostic parameters for evaluating soil mineral fractions.

hasPart.name: 3.3 Data analysis and evaluation
hasPart.description: This subsection integrates field, laboratory, and spatial data to evaluate overall peatland characteristics. It bridges raw analytical findings with practical environmental assessments.

hasPart.name: 3.3.1 Land use assessment in verified peatland areas
hasPart.description: This subsection assesses how current land uses interact with and impact the newly verified peatland zones. It identifies anthropogenic pressures and potential degradation risks.

hasPart.name: 3.3.2 Peatland demarcation refinement and boundary
hasPart.description: This subsection discusses the process of refining peatland boundaries based on empirical ground data. It establishes corrected spatial limits replacing generalized regional estimates.

hasPart.name: 3.3.3 Peat soil layer depth classification
hasPart.description: This subsection classifies the verified peat deposits according to their measured vertical depths. It categorizes the spatial distribution of shallow and deep peat layers.

hasPart.name: Results
hasPart.description: This section synthesizes key empirical outcomes regarding soil depth classifications and preliminary spatial findings. It bridges laboratory data with overarching environmental evaluations.

hasPart.name: 3.4 Geospatial mapping and GIS assessment
hasPart.description: This subsection utilizes GIS tools to model and visualize the spatial characteristics of the verified peatlands. It generates comprehensive maps illustrating the refined geographical distributions.

hasPart.name: 3.4.1 Comparative analysis: IMDGNP vs verified boundaries
hasPart.description: This subsection compares the discrepancies between official IMDGNP map estimates and the empirically verified peat boundaries. It quantifies the spatial variances and mapping inaccuracies.

hasPart.name: 3.4.2 Final demarcation mapping products
hasPart.description: This subsection presents the final cartographic outputs resulting from the refined geospatial analysis. These high-accuracy maps serve as a reliable reference for regional planning and conservation.

hasPart.name: 4. CONCLUSION
hasPart.description: This section summarizes the primary findings of the study, emphasizing the necessity of updating official peatland maps using empirical geospatial verification. It offers recommendations for policy adjustments and future environmental management in the Pontianak Delta.
